# D23/D24 construction and hidden-allocation review

> **Research only.** Every proposal below requires user approval before code application. This file was generated mechanically from the pinned TypeScript export graph, pinned Rust source, and matching Rust API manifests.

## Decision digest

Counts below are recomputed findings, not target quotas. The digest proposes review rules; it does not approve any contract change or drop any row from the appendices.

### Corrected Entity detection

**Proposed rule:** Entity iff Rust source has a direct EntityRuntimeSlot, a concrete embedded *Fields path to one, an explicit Entity impl/supertrait, or an invocation of a macro whose definition expands an Entity impl TypeScript unions do not acquire a runtime merely because one alternative is an Entity; non-union aliases/intersections follow only their top-level base identity.

| Measure | Returned artifact | Regenerated artifact |
|---|---:|---:|
| tsRustEntityDisagreements | 520 | 245 |
| missingCreate | 325 | 169 |
| missingInitialize | 410 | 238 |
| ambiguousRows | 791 | 632 |
| constructionRows | 1022 | 869 |

The reductions remove manifest-only false disagreements and union/member-token false positives; remaining disagreements are retained for review (for example, TS-only families with no pinned Rust counterpart). Construction signatures are still counted exactly once.

No parser, reader, or string exemption is blanket.

## Mechanical notes

- Export reachability is the union of each package's resolved `src/index.ts` and `src/contract.ts` graph, including `export *`, selected re-exports, aliases, and local export lists.
- Entity evidence follows concrete Rust source fields, verified Entity-family macro definitions/invocations, explicit impls, and Entity supertraits. TypeScript unions do not inherit identity from member tokens.
- Category, defining-content, derived-state, detachability, and ownership classifications are proposals. Low-confidence cases are intentionally surfaced in the first section rather than silently treated as decisions.
- The JSON is the canonical machine-readable artifact. It includes overload arrays, exact source lines, diagnostics, hashes, hidden-allocation exclusions, and ambiguity records.
